exercises.prompt: Why does مَسَاجِدُ ('mosques') end in a single ḍammah rather than tanwīn (-un)?
choices: It follows the ultimate plural pattern مَفَاعِلُ, which is a diptote barred from tanwīn
It is in an iḍāfah construct
exercises.answer: It follows the ultimate plural pattern مَفَاعِلُ, which is a diptote barred from tanwīn
exercises.explanation: Broken plurals on مَفَاعِلُ and مَفَاعِيلُ are diptotes (al-mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) and never take tanwīn.

feedback.rule: Quadriliteral plural patterns مَفَاعِلُ and مَفَاعِيلُ are diptotes.

exercises.prompt: Match each singular noun to its broken plural.
exercises.explanation: مَسْجِدٌ → مَسَاجِدُ (مَفَاعِلُ), مِفْتَاحٌ → مَفَاتِيحُ (مَفَاعِيلُ), عَالِمٌ → عُلَمَاءُ (فُعَلَاءُ).

feedback.rule: Quadriliteral and human broken plural patterns

exercises.prompt: True or False: Human broken plurals such as عُلَمَاءُ ('scholars') are treated as feminine singular.
exercises.explanation: False. The feminine singular agreement rule applies to non-human plurals; rational human plurals take plural agreement.

feedback.rule: Human plurals agree in actual gender and plural number.
